clue.text: Monument — not cheap to be rebuilt

indicators.note: rebuilding puts the same materials back together in a new form, so the words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A costly monument is going to be reconstructed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cenotaph in Whitehall is the UK's chief war memorial.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph is a memorial to people buried elsewhere, a kind of monument.

clue.text: Prepare to shoot male bird

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to raise the hammer of a gun ready for firing
second meaning: a rooster or any male fowl

explanation.surface: A hunter readies the gun to bag a male bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one hunting scene, but the two halves are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: To cock a gun is to set its hammer for firing; a cock is also a male bird, especially a rooster.

clue.text: Flummox with puns on live broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast in its old sense means scattered about, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
L marks the live wire on an electrical plug

explanation.surface: A comedian baffles the audience with wordplay on a live show.
explanation.walkthrough: L for live comes from plug wiring (live, neutral, earth).
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to leave them so puzzled they cannot respond, the same as flummoxing them.

clue.text: I criticise doctor getting in cask for game

indicators.note: getting in means going inside something, so the earlier pieces sit within the cask

parts.note: a tun is a large barrel for wine or beer
taken as written
to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
standard abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to criticising a doctor who climbs into a barrel as a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Tip and run is a casual form of cricket in which the batter must run whenever the ball is hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tip and run is an informal cricket variant, a game played in parks and gardens.

clue.text: Control of expenditure may cause row in US — reps unhappy

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, here the row inside the jumbled letters
something unhappy is out of sorts, so these letters are knocked out of their order

parts.note: taken as written, six letters to be rearranged
a string is a row or series of things

explanation.surface: Control of spending sparks a quarrel in the US because congressmen are unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel to fit the political picture, but it means a line of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever holds the purse strings decides how money is spent, an idiom for financial control.

clue.text: Characteristic of stars attending Belfast rally

indicators.note: attending means being present at, so the word is present inside the following phrase

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Celebrities turn up at a political gathering in Belfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' suggests celebrities appearing at the rally, but it is the heavenly kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Astral is the adjective from the Latin for star, describing what relates to the stars.

clue.text: Kind of squash?

parts.note: surface reading: a variety of the vegetable, or a type of fruit drink or racket game
setter's reading: a way of crushing something flat, by bringing the foot down hard on it

explanation.walkthrough: Squash suggests a gourd, a drink or a sport; here it is the verb, and one way to squash is with the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To stamp on something is to crush it underfoot, a particular manner of squashing.

clue.text: Stopped working and went to bed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: left employment at the end of a career
second meaning: withdrew for the night

explanation.surface: Someone finished the day's work and turned in.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one tired person's evening; the two halves are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both giving up one's job for good and, more formally, going off to sleep.

clue.text: A lot to say, possibly, after end of meal and this?

definitions.text: A lot to say, possibly, after end of meal and this?

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible arrangement among many of the letters given

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of meal

explanation.surface: After a formal dinner comes this, and with it plenty of speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and description: after dinner a toast to the monarch is drunk, followed by speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: The loyal toast, to the sovereign, is proposed at the end of a formal dinner before speeches begin.

clue.text: Plot to deceive summit

parts.note: to con someone is to trick them
a spire is a tapering top, as on a church

explanation.surface: A scheme to mislead delegates at a summit meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summit' suggests a diplomatic meeting, but it is a peak, a pointed top.
explanation.definitionFit: To conspire is to plot secretly together; the verb sense of plot matches it.

clue.text: Somewhat inexperienced driver included in team

indicators.note: included in means held within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a party is a group working together, as in a search party
L is the learner plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A rather green driver has been picked for the team.
explanation.walkthrough: Learner drivers in Britain display L-plates, hence L.
explanation.definitionFit: Partly means to some extent, not wholly, the same as somewhat.

clue.text: Injured from same rash wrestler's blow?

indicators.note: something injured is damaged and bent out of shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written, twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wrestler hurt by the same skin rash asks whether it was a blow.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is by example: this is one blow a wrestler might use.
explanation.definitionFit: A forearm smash is a strike with the forearm, a move used in professional wrestling.

clue.text: NCO in open car with collar undone

indicators.note: something undone has come apart, so the letters fall into another order

parts.note: taken as written, the link 'with' joining the two words of fodder

explanation.surface: A non-commissioned officer drives a convertible with his shirt collar unbuttoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' here is part of the fodder phrase, its letters are not used; the anagram takes open car collar.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance corporal is the lowest non-commissioned rank in the British Army, so is an NCO.

clue.text: Suntanned solicitor catching river fish

parts.note: suntanned skin is brown

indicators.note: catching means holding something within, so one piece takes in the other

parts.note: a tout solicits custom or sells tickets
standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A tanned lawyer lands a fish from the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests a British lawyer, but here it is literally one who solicits, a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: The brown trout is a common European freshwater game fish.

clue.text: One getting up out of chair is erudite

indicators.note: out of means taken from within, so the word is lifted from the following phrase

parts.note: the letters span the end of chair, all of is and the start of erudite

explanation.surface: A learned professor stands up from a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chair' suggests a professor's post, fitting erudite, but it only houses the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A riser is someone who gets out of bed, as in an early riser.

clue.text: Worth it, reading a Poe novel, or an Orwell documentary

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, eighteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Is it better to read a novel by Poe or an Orwell nonfiction book?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a noun, a Poe book, but it is the adjective new, signalling the rearrangement. Wigan is a town in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's 1937 book reports on working-class poverty in northern England, a work of documentary journalism.

clue.text: Old man after drop of 'nectar' ready to be served from the barrel

definitions.text: ready to be served from the barrel

indicators.note: after places one piece to follow the other in the answer

parts.note: standard abbreviation for old

indicators.note: a drop is the smallest amount, so only the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the first letter of nectar
a man is a playing piece in draughts (checkers), also called a draught

explanation.surface: An old fellow after a sip of good beer, ready to pour from the cask.
explanation.walkthrough: Draughts is the British name for checkers, whose pieces are called men.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer on draught is drawn straight from the cask or keg rather than bottled.

clue.text: See 15
Old woman on river with Spanish nobleman

parts.note: gran is short for grandmother
the Dee is a river in Scotland, and another in Wales and England

explanation.surface: An elderly woman by a river with a Spanish aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the first piece sits on top of the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee was a Spanish or Portuguese nobleman of the highest rank.

clue.text: Garment for groom

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a one-piece item of clothing for a woman

explanation.surface: An outfit chosen for the bridegroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' suggests a wedding, but it is the verb to tidy or prepare.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a garment as a noun and, as a verb, to prepare or tidy, like grooming.

clue.text: Make flat cool, abroad

parts.note: cool in temper is even, as in even-tempered
abroad means out and about, away from home

explanation.surface: An instruction to lower a flat's temperature while away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like an apartment to be cooled; it belongs to the definition with 'Make'.
explanation.definitionFit: To even out a surface is to level it, removing bumps, which is to make it flat.

clue.text: Started eating out where the industrial firms are concentrated?

definitions.text: where the industrial firms are concentrated?

indicators.note: out here means put out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, thirteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: People began dining out in the district where businesses cluster.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a descriptive definition rather than a dictionary one.
explanation.definitionFit: A trading estate is a planned area of land set aside for factories and warehouses, a British term for an industrial park.

clue.text: One judge, very angry

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
to rate something is to assess or judge it

explanation.surface: A single judge is furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' reads as a person, but it is the verb to assess.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means full of anger, a synonym of very angry.

clue.text: You need to sow, reportedly, to yield

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word is judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: to seed a field is to sow it

explanation.surface: Advice that a gardener must plant in order to get a crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yield' suggests a harvest, fitting the sowing, but it means to give way.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to give up or surrender something, such as territory, which is to yield it.

clue.text: Out-of-date, so not the gear for Ascot?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, taken literally: worn headgear, unfit for a racecourse where new hats are paraded

explanation.surface: Something passé, so unsuitable to wear at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Ascot is an English horse-racing meeting famous for its extravagant hats.
explanation.definitionFit: Old hat is an idiom for tired and unoriginal, and literally a worn hat.

clue.text: Evergreen provides chap a little wood

parts.note: a chap is a man
a grove is a small wood

explanation.surface: A tree gives a fellow some timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evergreen' reads as an adjective but it is the noun, a tree that keeps its leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The mangrove is a tropical tree of tidal swamps that keeps its foliage all year.

clue.text: Goddess captured in outskirts of this ancient city

indicators.note: captured in means held inside, so the goddess goes between the kept letters
outskirts are the edges of a town, so only the outer letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of this
Hebe was the Greek goddess of youth

explanation.surface: A goddess was taken prisoner on the edges of an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' points at the answer itself, so its outer letters wrap the goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a major city of ancient Egypt, and also of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Chess player at match in formal evening dress

parts.note: one side in chess plays the white pieces
a tie is a match, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: A chess competitor turns up to the match in a dinner suit.
explanation.walkthrough: In British sport a cup tie is a knockout match.
explanation.definitionFit: White tie, a tailcoat with white bow tie, is the most formal evening dress code.
